# Explicit Addressing — selecting a KB from inside and outside it, the removed
# registry commands, and the absent home registry file.

exec akb init kb-one
stdout 'Initialized KB .kb-one.'
! exists $HOME/.config/agent-kb/registry.yaml

exec akb init kb-two
stdout 'Initialized KB .kb-two.'
! exists $HOME/.config/agent-kb/registry.yaml

# Inside a KB the harness selection (AKB_KB=.) addresses it.
cd kb-one

# init seeds no templates: copy the one this scenario writes pages of.
exec akb template get note --full --examples
cp stdout .agent-kb/templates/note.yaml
exec git add .agent-kb/templates
exec git commit -m 'seed note template'

stdin ../note-input.md
exec akb write my-note.md
stdout 'Written to kb/notes/my-note.md'

exec akb read notes/my-note.md
stdout 'Note content.'

exec akb list
stdout 'notes/my-note.md'

exec akb search test
stdout 'notes/my-note.md'

exec akb status
stdout 'Name: kb-one'

# Outside any KB, the flag selects one explicitly.
cd $WORK
exec akb --kb kb-one status
stdout 'Name: kb-one'

# The flag wins over a conflicting environment selection.
env AKB_KB=kb-two
exec akb --kb kb-one status
stdout 'Name: kb-one'

# Without any selection the invocation is a usage mistake that lists the
# nearby bases.
env AKB_KB=
! exec akb status
stderr 'usage: resolve knowledge base: no knowledge base selected'
stderr '(?s)discovered knowledge bases \(nearest first\):.*  kb-one  .*  kb-two  '

# The removed registry commands are unknown commands.
! exec akb use kb-one
stderr 'unknown command "use"'
! exec akb registry
stderr 'unknown command "registry"'

-- note-input.md --
---
type: note
title: Explicit Addressing Test Note
summary: A test note
tags: test
---
Note content.
